stories.title: Canada's OSFI: tokenized deposits have the same legal character as ordinary deposits
stories.summary: Canada's financial regulator issued a statement (10 Sep) saying tokenized or digitally represented deposits are 'not legally distinct from traditional deposits' - the legal character follows the product, not the rail. For builders this removes a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction ambiguity: a bank's tokenized deposit liability is still a deposit, so existing deposit rules and expectations keep applying. Caveat: it is a supervisory statement, not legislation - B-13 (cyber) and B-10 (third-party risk) still apply and firms must clear launches with their OSFI supervisor. Publication time is date-only (10 Sep); using noon Ottawa time.

quality.note: Official OSFI statement page, verified live; X post surfaced it in-window.

stories.title: UK Lords amend Financial Services and Markets Bill to mandate a statutory digital-asset strategy
stories.summary: The House of Lords' Report-stage amendments to the Financial Services and Markets Bill [HL] now include Clause 50: within 12 months of Royal Assent, HM Treasury must prepare, publish and consult on a strategy covering cryptoassets, qualifying stablecoins, CBDCs, tokenized securities and related financial market infrastructure. The amended bill text was published on bills.parliament.uk on 10 Sep. Caveat: the Commons can still reject Lords amendments, and a parallel 'Amendment 164' with similar text was listed as not moved - this is a committee-stage insertion, not enacted law.

stories.title: Updated CLARITY Act text released ahead of 15 Sep Senate cloture vote
stories.summary: Sen. Lummis released substitute text for the Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act the night before the 15 Sep cloture vote, with stated changes on when 'decentralized-in-name-only' protocols must register with the CFTC/BSA, a DeFi safe harbor limited to spot/cash digital commodities, and credit-union digital-asset powers; Lummis claims 114+ Democratic-requested edits were addressed. CoinDesk reports the draft is not the ethics compromise Democrats have demanded and that 60 votes are not assured. stories.title: ECDSA.Fail: open challenge cuts secp256k1 Shor-attack spacetime cost by 50%+ (arXiv 2609.09582)
stories.summary: An open 'autoresearch' challenge (submitted 9 Sep, arXiv 2609.09582) cut the spacetime cost of reversible secp256k1 point addition - a Shor's-algorithm bottleneck - by 86.1% versus the contest baseline and more than 50% below Google Quantum AI's March published score; best circuit: 1,151 logical qubits, ~1.30M Toffoli gates. Authors span Theta Labs, Ethereum Foundation, StarkWare, Starknet Foundation and Trail of Bits. Caveat: it optimizes one sub-step of the attack, not a full Shor estimate; the comparison with Google is not like-for-like, and no current machine can run it at cryptographic scale.

quality.note: arXiv preprint with exposed v1 submission timestamp; reported in-window by CoinDesk and by a StarkWare blog post.

stories.title: Zodia Custody CEO steps down as Standard Chartered custody split advances
stories.summary: Julian Sawyer steps down as CEO of Standard Chartered-backed Zodia Custody to become an adviser, with Richard Clark leading the custody transition. The structure being unwound puts custody toward Standard Chartered while Zodia Solutions continues as infrastructure. For builders: institutional custody consolidation is changing which names to integrate with and which hold the regulated perimeter. Caveat: the acquisition is not closed and remains subject to regulatory approvals - this is a personnel/process story, not a completed deal.

quality.note: Single reporting outlet (CoinDesk) in-window; official company statement not yet retrieved. Deal explicitly not closed.

stories.title: Anthropic publishes its most detailed AI misuse report to date (September 2026)
stories.summary: Anthropic released 'Countering misuse of AI: September 2026,' the most detailed misuse report it has published, covering cyber, influence, surveillance, weapons, bio, fraud and illicit distillation (including large chain-of-thought-extraction campaigns) across Dec 2025 - Aug 2026, and says it disrupted every listed operation. For builders: it is the best public catalogue of how frontier models are actually misused, and which model families appear in each attack class. Caveat: cases are selected 'most sophisticated,' not typical traffic, and attribution plus uplift claims are Anthropic's own; the report names Haiku/Sonnet/Opus, with Fable/Mythos in only one distillation case.

quality.note: Official Anthropic page and PDF, verified live; announced via @AnthropicAI in-window.

stories.title: GPT-Live-1 is GA on the API: full-duplex voice, $0.05/min, 83.6% Tau3 with Astra
stories.summary: OpenAI took gpt-live-1 general-availability on v1/live/sessions - a full-duplex voice layer that listens while speaking and delegates reasoning/tools to a backend (Astra, Terra, Codex or client-side). OpenAI reports Tau3 pass@1 83.6% with Astra medium vs 45.7% for GPT-Realtime-2.1, reply start 0.798s vs 1.41s, and prices it at $0.05/min billed per second. For builders: this is the lowest-latency path to agents that talk and act simultaneously, with a clean session API. Caveat: it is not a new pretrain (shipped in ChatGPT 2026-07-08; this is API GA), the headline Tau3 number is the voice model plus GPT-6 Astra, not the voice model alone, and rate limits are concurrent sessions, not tokens.

quality.note: Official OpenAI page + developer docs, verified live; announced via @OpenAIDevs in-window.

stories.title: Runway details how to turn Gen-4.5-class models into real-time, streaming video generation
stories.summary: Runway published a technical write-up on 'instant' video: converting Gen-4.5-class models to causal autoregressive generation, then off-policy and on-policy distribution-matching distillation so frames stream with low time-to-first-frame, positioning instant generation as the path for interactive worlds, agents and robotics. For builders: a concrete recipe for making video models run interactively rather than batch. Caveat: it is a research overview, not a public model drop - Solaris and GWM Worlds 2 were announced last week (outside this window), and a thread reply notes those were 'announced more than released.'

stories.title: Unitree open-sources UnifoLM-WLA-1.0: 6B-parameter humanoid VLA on ~2,500 hours of real-robot data

stories.title: Dixit lab: cysteine reduction, not methionine restriction, drives the survival benefit (bioRxiv)
stories.summary: Orliaguet, Kim, Dixit et al. (Yale/Cologne, posted 9 Sep, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.04.749519v1) split the classic methionine-restriction longevity story: cysteine-free diets extend survival even when methionine is replete, while methionine restriction with normal cysteine does not; a sustained ~70% cysteine reduction in aged Cth-/- mice reprograms immunometabolism and improves healthspan. For builders: if you track dietary geroprotection, the actionable variable may be cysteine, not methionine. Evidence is animal (C. elegans lifespan/stress plus cysteine-synthesis-deficient mice), not human; preprint, not peer-reviewed, and no clinical trial is announced.

quality.note: bioRxiv preprint page verified live, v1 posted 9 Sep 2026 (date-only; noon UTC used per policy). Preprint - animal evidence only.

stories.title: LINE-1 transcription alone rewires primary human fibroblast omics (bioRxiv)
stories.summary: Bravo, Benayoun et al. (USC/Buck Institute, posted 8 Sep, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.09.03.749265v1) show that acute LINE-1 overexpression rewires the transcriptome, proteome and secretome of primary human IMR-90 fibroblasts - testing whether L1 transcription itself, not full senescence, is enough to remodel the cell. The authors say the pattern is not a simple SASP/antiviral signature. For builders: a mechanistic datapoint on one of the central senescence hallmarks, in human cells. Caveat: one fibroblast line, transient overexpression, no in vivo lifespan or human intervention data; preprint, not peer-reviewed.

quality.note: bioRxiv preprint page verified live, v1 posted 8 Sep 2026 (date-only; noon UTC used per policy). Human-cell in vitro evidence; preprint.

stories.title: Catch-up: Genflow's SIRT6 gene therapy meets primary endpoint in aged beagles (SLAB)
stories.summary: Genflow Biosciences announced (8 Sep, BioSpace/ACCESS Newswire) that its SLAB (Sarcopenia and Longevity in Aged Beagles) trial of the SIRT6 centenarian gene therapy met its primary endpoint - reducing biological age as measured by the GRIM methylation clock, with treated aged dogs showing clear improvement versus controls. For builders: the first gene-therapy readout where the primary endpoint itself is an aging clock, in a large animal cohort. Evidence is animal (24 aged beagles), not human; detailed data are deferred to the ALOS meeting in Toronto, 1-2 Oct 2026.

quality.note: Press release dated 8 Sep 2026 (date-only; noon UTC used per policy), corroborated by two outlets; recirculated in-window on X. Included as catch-up: canonical URL absent from current edition and archives.

stories.title: Catch-up: first patient dosed in GENESIS-IPF-3 - Phase III of the first AI-discovered drug
stories.summary: Insilico Medicine announced (9 Sep, PR Newswire) that it dosed the first patient in GENESIS-IPF-3 (NCT07687459), a 52-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase III of rentosertib in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, with Peking Union Medical College Hospital and Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital enrolling the same day; 320 patients across 47 China centers, primary endpoint the annual rate of FVC decline. For builders: the generative-AI drug-discovery loop now has a pivotal-trial-scale readout to watch - first Phase III of an AI-discovered small molecule. Caveat: first-patient-in, not efficacy; it is an IPF efficacy trial, not a longevity trial, and the clock findings belong to the 7 Sep Nature Biotechnology paper already in this paper's archive.

quality.note: PR Newswire release dated 9 Sep 2026 (date-only; noon UTC used per policy), amplified on X in-window by @InSilicoMeds and @biogerontology. Included as catch-up: PR date falls in the 72-hour sweep and the canonical URL was absent from the current edition.
